_comment: Durable human decisions about individual accounts, keyed by venue name.
The merge, geocode and routing passes are all regenerable from the research
sweeps, and re-running them must not quietly discard a judgement someone
made. Anything decided by a person rather than computed lives here and is
Each entry says who decided, when, and why. An override without a reason is
_merge_comment: Pairs the matcher surfaced for review and a human then decided. Each entry
folds the listed names into the first one. The matcher stays conservative on
purpose — a false merge deletes a real prospect and nobody notices — so these
are the cases where a person looked and confirmed.
Pairs deliberately NOT merged, and why:
The Savoy / The George Limerick — one collection, two real properties.
Two accounts with one buyer. Handled by the group rule, not by merging.
Listowel Arms / The Cliff House — same, and both outside the ring anyway.
Hotel Doolin / Doolin Inn — shared ownership unconfirmed; outside the ring.
Bunratty Castle Hotel / Bunratty Manor Hotel — different businesses, one village.
Dromoland Castle / The Rine — different venues on one estate.

Slieve Aughty Centre.reason: One venue listed under three names across directories.

Greenhills Hotel.reason: One Ennis Road property; the hotel uses both names interchangeably on its own site. In-ring, so a duplicate would waste an outreach slot.

The George Hotel Limerick.reason: One Limerick city property under two word orders. Its weddings route to the Savoy, which stays a separate account in the same collection.

Lahinch Coast Hotel & Suites.reason: Same property; ampersand versus the word.

The Thatched Cottage.reason: Restaurant and bar with a banquet room. D-012 excludes restaurants and pubs explicitly.

St. John's Church, Knockainey.reason: Ceremony venue only, no reception. Cannot sponsor a couple experience.

The Bedford Townhouse & Café.reason: Twenty-four guests and no wedding marketing of its own. Fails the coordinator and calendar tests.

Ballyneety Golf Club.reason: Has function capacity but markets no weddings. Fails the coordinator test.

The George Hotel Limerick.reason: No wedding page, no function room, no events page. Its own collection's site routes weddings to the Savoy, which is a separate account. The directory listing quotes the Savoy's bedroom count and suite capacity, so it is sister-hotel data rather than a venue.
The George Hotel Limerick.decided_by: Claude Code, verified on the venue's own site

Woodfield House Hotel.reason: The word wedding does not appear anywhere on its site, its events page reads 'no upcoming events', and the domain a directory sends couples to does not resolve. Fails the coordinator and calendar tests.
Woodfield House Hotel.decided_by: Claude Code, verified on the venue's own site

The Savoy Collection (Limerick city hote.reason: Not a venue. A research sweep recorded the collection itself as an account alongside its member hotels, which are already in the universe separately.

Kilmurry Lodge Hotel.reason: Directories carry a 230 capacity, a one-wedding-a-day policy and a coordinator; none of it appears on the hotel's own site, where 'wedding' occurs once, as 'Wedding Day 2s' for the terrace. The conflict is recorded rather than resolved — this needs a phone call, not a judgement.
Kilmurry Lodge Hotel.decided_by: Claude Code, conflict recorded per WORKFLOWS section 8

Limerick Racecourse (Greenmount Park).reason: Markets wedding packages with real banqueting capacity, but a racecourse is not one of the six D-012 types. Founder call.

Thomond Park Stadium.reason: Five wedding suites and a civil-ceremony licence is a real weddings operation, but a stadium is not one of the six D-012 types. Founder call.

Cratloe Woods House.reason: Not a wedding venue. The claim traces aggregator to aggregator and never reaches a first-party source; the historic-houses database records it as a private home, its domain does not resolve, it appears on no wedding directory, and a local heritage piece says it was once open to the public in the past tense.

_groups_comment: Ownership the research recorded as independent and a closer look showed is not.
This matters twice. It drops decision_access, because the decision moves up to
group level. And it triggers the one-property-per-operator cohort rule, without
which one buyer receives three personalised films in the same week — the exact
impression a personalised film exists to avoid.
It also cuts the other way, and the packet says so: one group conversation
could land three founding venues at once.

Castle Oaks House Hotel.reason: Six-property group with unified booking and, per the group's own site, wedding services coordinated jointly across locations. Recorded as independent by the first pass.

Castletroy Park Hotel.reason: Same group. Recorded as independent by the first pass.

Charleville Park Hotel.reason: Same group. Recorded as independent by the first pass.

Limerick Strand Hotel.reason: Fourteen-property collection, not an independent hotel. Note for a later pass: SHR appears on its booking flow and is booking software, not an owner — do not record it as the operator.

Radisson Blu Hotel & Spa Limerick.reason: Operated by Inua Hospitality under the Radisson brand, corroborated by its brochure being published on the group's own account. Two layers above the property, not locally operated.

Limerick Strand Hotel.reason: Listed on OpenStreetMap as The Strand Hotel, so the venue name alone would not resolve.

Cahermoyle House.reason: Venue would not resolve; Ardagh centroid used. Ring-usable, NOT film-usable.

Smithstown Castle.reason: Caught by venue-coord-audit. The geocoder matched the name to Smithstown Industrial Estate in Shannon — right county, right first word, wrong side of it — and the venue entered Cohort 1 at 26.8 minutes. It is at Kilshanny in west Clare, well over an hour out. Kilshanny centroid used; the account routes out of the ring.

Treacys Oakwood Hotel (Oak Wood Arms).reason: Caught by venue-coord-audit sitting on Smithstown Industrial Estate. The drive time was about right because the estate is in Shannon, but the point was not the hotel — which matters for E13.17's film render even where it does not change the ring.

Lisheen Castle.reason: Caught by venue-coord-audit resolving into County Cork, roughly 100 km from the recorded address at Moyne, Thurles. Moyne centroid used. Outside the ring either way.

The Black Castle (Tullaun Castle).reason: Venue would not resolve; Nenagh centroid used. Ring-usable, NOT film-usable.

Fota Island Clubhouse.reason: Cork, no coordinate and no town recorded. Far outside the ring on county alone.

Inish Beg Estate.reason: West Cork. Far outside the ring on county alone.

The Galmont Hotel & Spa.reason: Galway city. Far outside the ring on county alone.

The Brehon Hotel & Spa.reason: Killarney. Far outside the ring on county alone.

The Killarney Park Hotel.reason: Killarney. Far outside the ring on county alone.

The Manor West Hotel.reason: Tralee. Far outside the ring on county alone.
